text: When you design a REST API, clear and consistent endpoints are essential. Use nouns for resources and HTTP methods to describe actions. Always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened. For example, use 200 for success, 201 for creation, and 404 when a resource is missing. Good documentation helps developers use your API quickly and avoid mistakes. Versioning is also important because it allows you to improve your API without breaking existing applications. By following these best practices, you can build APIs that are easy to use, maintain, and scale over time.
